summary: Ainos, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing a September 24, 2026 Global Exclusive License Agreement with Taiwan's BioPhoenix Co., Ltd. covering the VELDONA low-dose oral interferon alpha platform for Sjögren's Disease and Thrombocytopenia worldwide. BioPhoenix pays a $600,000 upfront fee, a first-sublicense fee, and up to roughly $10.0 million total if all additional VELDONA indications are licensed, plus 25% of net sublicensing revenue. The term runs per indication/country to the later of last patent expiry or 20 years, with a 10-year non-compete and a right of first refusal/call option on Phase 2 indications. Watch technology-transfer completion triggering the upfront fee and any sublicense economics.
